name: Pale Greyish Vinaceous
lede: Pale Greyish Vinaceous is a pale, dusty pink with a wine-like cast, one of Ridgway's 1912 "vinaceous" family of names built from the Latin word for wine.

sections.title: A wine-toned pink
sections.body:
Ridgway coined his vinaceous terms from *vinaceus*, Latin for wine-colored, to describe pinks with a greyish or purplish cast rather than a clear rose [1]. This shade sits on plate XXXIX, hue 9''', tone f, of his 1912 standards, read from a scan of an aged plate [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system lists the same area as block 10, "pale yellowish pink," about 4.9 units from this exact color [1]. Its Munsell notation is 3.8YR 8.1/2.2 [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[iris-mauve]], [[sandust]], [[pale-congo-pink]] and [[tussore]], at 2.6, 3.5, 3.7 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. Who used the color beyond Ridgway's plates is undocumented in the books we hold [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this pink appears in 489, about 2.1 percent, more common than 78 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 54 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.1 times the expected rate, and it is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.5 times the expected rate [2].

Inside a painting it is most often a light [2]. The earliest match is a 900 painting by Zhao Guangfu, over a thousand years before Ridgway's 1912 name, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a trace of this named pink, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[light-brownish-drab]] and [[hay-s-brown|Hay's Brown]] [2].
